nodes.title: classify.js distressCheck, which runs on the outage, unreadable, stray-script and model-failure paths, still reads a content-filter block by the hate detectors alone as distress (fail closed). 14.4 made the reply probe (wordsTrip) and the across-deployment read (distressAcross) treat a hate-only block as no child-safety signal. Not this path, for two reasons. First, nothing has measured bullying lines that quote the slurs said to the child; the 276-line distress battery has none, and on the probe 0 of its lines were hate-only. Second, on this path a fail-closed read carries no sureBy, so state.js checkTier sends it to the gentle check-in, never the helpline script. A false positive costs one 'are you okay' and does not bring back the helpline over-firing. Reverse if real-lesson traces show a hate-only block here firing a check-in on a harmless line (e.g. a history answer), AND a bullying battery quoting slurs shows the predicate or the other reads still catch those lines without it.

md.decisions:
## dc-r1441-distresscheck-hate-stays-closed — the outage-path distress read keeps a hate block as a check-in (2026-10-21)

The reply probe and the across-deployment read stopped treating a hate-only filter block as distress in 14.4. The rare outage-path read still does, because no one has measured bullying lines that quote slurs. Here a fail-closed read is only a gentle check-in, never the helpline script.
